title: Week 4 — Working with Real Economic Data Using Pandas
text:
Weeks 1–3 built:

computational confidence
Python fundamentals
programming logic

Now students begin real data analysis.
This is one of the most important weeks in the entire course.
Why?
Because in real-world economics:
data is almost never clean
Professional economists spend enormous amounts of time:

cleaning data
restructuring data
handling missing values
checking consistency
merging datasets
creating variables

Poor data handling destroys analysis long before models matter.

title: Week 2 — Working with Data in Python
text:
In Week 1, we learned how to use Python as a calculator and how to execute simple commands.
This week, we begin working with the most important asset in modern economics:
DATA
Every day economists use data to answer questions such as:

Why are some people unemployed?
What determines wages?
Why does inflation increase?
Which districts experience higher poverty?
How does education affect earnings?
How does technology influence productivity?

Regardless of whether you become:

an economist
policy analyst
researcher
consultant
banker
data analyst

your ability to work with data will become increasingly important.
For this reason, Week 2 focuses on understanding how Python stores and organizes data.
Everything we do later in the course:

data visualization
dashboards
forecasting
machine learning
artificial intelligence

depends on concepts introduced this week.

title: Week 3 — Programming Logic and Automation for Economic Analysis
text:
Economic Example: Inflation Classification



Component
Example




Input
Inflation rate


Rule
Below 5 is low; 5–15 is moderate; above 15 is high


Process
Compare the observed rate with each threshold


Output
Inflation classification



Before writing code, an analyst should be able to explain the rule clearly in words.

title: Week 3 — Programming Logic and Automation for Economic Analysis
text:
Try It
inflation = 12

print(inflation > 10)
print(inflation < 5)
print(inflation == 12)

title: Week 3 — Programming Logic and Automation for Economic Analysis
text:
Example: Labour Force Classification
has_job = False
seeking_work = True

if not has_job and seeking_work:
    print("Unemployed")

title: Week 3 — Programming Logic and Automation for Economic Analysis
text:
Example: Policy Alert
inflation = 18
growth = -2

if inflation > 15 or growth < 0:
    print("Macroeconomic policy attention required")

title: Week 3 — Programming Logic and Automation for Economic Analysis
text:
Interpretation
The value 12 is:

not below 5
less than or equal to 15

Therefore, Python returns:
Moderate inflation

title: Week 3 — Programming Logic and Automation for Economic Analysis
text:
Critical Note
This is a simplified monetary classification.
Real poverty analysis may also consider:

household size
cost-of-living differences
access to education and health
housing conditions
multidimensional deprivation

Code can automate a rule, but the analyst must evaluate whether the rule is appropriate.

title: Week 3 — Programming Logic and Automation for Economic Analysis
text:
Important Distinction
Loops are valuable for learning programming logic.
For large DataFrames, later lessons will introduce more efficient pandas methods.

Objective
Visualize the relationship between two variables.

title: Week 5 In-Class Activity
text:
Instructions
Create scatter plot using:

inflation
exchange rate change

title: Week 5 In-Class Activity
text:
Example Structure
plt.scatter(data["Inflation"],
            data["Exchange_Rate_Change"])

plt.xlabel("Inflation")
plt.ylabel("Exchange Rate Change")

plt.show()

title: Week 5 In-Class Activity
text:
Questions

Question 1
Do the variables appear related?



Question 2
Are there outliers?



Question 3
Why are scatter plots useful in economics?

Problem 1 — Missing Labels
Graphs without:

titles
axis labels
units

are poor analytical practice.

title: Week 5 In-Class Activity
text:
Problem 2 — Misinterpreting Correlation
Correlation indicates association.
It does NOT automatically indicate causation.

title: Week 5 In-Class Activity
text:
Problem 3 — Wrong Graph Choice
Different graph types answer different analytical questions.
Choose graphs based on analytical purpose.

Problem 4 — Ignoring Outliers
Extreme observations can distort:

averages
correlations
interpretations

Always inspect data visually.
